title: Appeals and Grievances Policy Manual: Filing Deadlines and Manner of Filing
content:
This part of the **Appeals and Grievances** policy manual governs when a case is in time and how it may be filed.

## Clauses

**1. Grievances and time-limited cases.** A grievance may be filed at any time; an appeal, hearing request or external review must be filed within its deadline.

**2. Source of the notice date.** The notice date is always taken from the decision's own notice record or from the plan appeal's resolution notice, never from the member's recollection. The decision's own notice record is the decision record held under Prior Authorization, the formulary exception or pharmacy prior authorization request held under the Pharmacy Benefit, or the adjudicated claim held under the Medicaid Managed Care Membership. The notice is the one for the decision reference the case is about, and the check is made on the plan's records before the case is accepted.

**3. The deadline.** An appeal, hearing request or external review is accepted only when filed no later than the case type's filing deadline, in calendar days, after the date on the notice being appealed. For a Standard Appeal or an Expedited Appeal the notice being appealed is the adverse benefit determination notice; for a State Fair Hearing or an External Medical Review it is the plan appeal's resolution notice.

**4. Counting.** The filing days are counted in calendar days from the day after the notice date, and a case filed on the last day is in time. The first counted day is the day after the notice date; the last counted day is the deadline figure's day; filing on that day or earlier is in time, filing on any later day is not.

**5. Late cases.** A late appeal is not accepted; the member may file a grievance about the matter instead.

**6. Manner of filing.** Filing is free, may be made orally through any channel in the case type's filing channels, and never needs a written follow-up.

## Worked boundary cases (hypothetical dates and deadlines)

| Notice date on record | Hypothetical deadline | Counted day 1 | Last day in time | Filed on | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 March | 60 calendar days | 2 March | 30 April | 30 April | In time |
| 1 March | 60 calendar days | 2 March | 30 April | 1 May | Late: not accepted |
| 1 June | 120 calendar days | 2 June | 29 September | 29 September | In time |
| 1 June | 120 calendar days | 2 June | 29 September | 30 September | Late: not accepted |

*Derivation for the first pair:* 2 to 31 March are 30 days and 1 to 30 April are 30 more, so the sixtieth day is 30 April. *For the second pair:* 2 to 30 June are 29 days, July brings the count to 60, August to 91, and 1 to 29 September to 120.

## Points of judgement

- **The member remembers a different notice date.** The date on the notice record governs; the member's recollection is never used.
- **A grievance filed long after the events.** A grievance has no deadline and is filed at any time.
- **An appeal found late.** It is not accepted, and the member may file a grievance about the matter instead.
- **A phone filing.** An oral filing through an accepted channel is complete; no written follow-up is ever needed, and no fee is charged.
